module8: Capstone: run an end-to-end change and audit the result
You now take one change from need to benefit and judge how well it went.
Frame one business need and agree what success looks like.
Run the steps: map, write stories, fit-gap, test, train.
Audit the result against the first need after 90 days.
Share lessons learned with the team.
A team asked for a new field, you found the real need was an approval step, and 90 days later approval time dropped from 4 days to 1. The audit also showed one report was still unused.
Take a small change through every step and write a short audit with lessons learned.
Audit compares results with the original need and lists at least three lessons.
quiz: A manager asks you to add a field for 'reason'. How do you find the real need?
Ask who needs it, what decision it supports and how often, and use the five whys. The real need may be a missing approval or report, not a field.
Your process map shows an order waiting 3 days in a queue and 2 hours being worked. What do you report?
That the wait time is the main problem, not the work time. Most of the delay is waiting between hand-offs, so improve those first.
Write one user story with an acceptance rule for a sales rep who wants reminders.
As a sales rep, I want a reminder 2 days before a quote expires so I can follow up. Accepted when a reminder appears exactly 2 days before expiry.
What do Must, Should and Could mean in a priority list?
Must items are needed for go-live, Should items are important but have a workaround, and Could items are nice to have if time allows.
Out of 50 requirements, 40 fit the standard features and 10 are gaps. What do you do next?
Use standard for the 40, then list options for each of the 10 with cost and risk. Choose to change the process, use a simple setting or build custom work.
Users run 10 test scripts and 3 fail. Can you ask for sign-off?
No. Log the 3 defects, fix them, and rerun those scripts (and any related ones) until they pass. Sign-off is given only on evidence that the tests pass.
The old system has 12,400 customers and the new one shows 12,150 after loading. What do you do?
Do not sign off. Reconcile the 250 missing records, find the reason such as duplicates or bad formats, and fix and reload until the counts match or differences are explained.
Name two parts of a good training plan.
Training matched to each role and champions in each team who help colleagues. Go-live support and follow-up checks also help.
How would you measure benefits 90 days after go-live?
Compare numbers set before the project, such as approval time or support calls, with the numbers now. Also check how many people actually use the new feature.
In your audit, the approval time did not improve. What do you do?
Find out why, such as users working around the new step or poor training, and report it honestly. Then agree a fix and record the lesson for future projects.
ladder: L1 Basic: Know the words
Remember key terms: stakeholder, requirement, user story, process map and acceptance test. Say what each one means in plain words.
Use a simple shop example for each term. Check the learner can give one example back. Common mistake: using requirement and solution as the same word.
L2 Awareness: See the flow of work
Understand the path from need to benefit and where an analyst helps. Explain why asking questions comes before building.
Draw the path on one page. Ask what happens if a step is skipped. Common mistake: jumping to a solution on day one.
L3 Foundation: Ask and draw
Apply interview questions and swim lane maps to one real process. Write a need in one clear sentence.
Run a short mock interview. Check the map shows waits and hand-offs. Common mistake: drawing how it should work instead of how it works.
L4 Practitioner: Write and fit
Apply stories with acceptance rules and build a fit-gap table. Analyse each gap for cost and risk.
Give a messy request and ask for ten stories. Check each is testable. Common mistake: stories that are too large to test.
L5 Specialist: Prove and migrate
Analyse test results and data loads. Evaluate whether a solution is ready for users to sign off.
Ask for the reconciliation table. Check defects are logged and closed. Common mistake: signing off on feelings, not evidence.
L6 Advanced: Lead adoption
Evaluate training and change plans against measures. Create an adoption plan with owners and dates.
Review the plan for measures. Check each team has a champion. Common mistake: ending the project at go-live.
L7 Super expert: Audit and coach
Create an end-to-end approach and audit the results against the first need. Evaluate lessons and teach others to use them.
Ask for a 90-day audit and a lessons list. Check the learner can coach a new analyst. Common mistake: celebrating delivery without checking benefit.
